title: Cost Signal Aggregator and Safe Batch Suggester
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Implement a cost-aware signal aggregation layer that encodes per-workload temporal and distributional features to drive continuous batching parameter recommendations. The component should prioritize safe config applies using staged rollouts, simulation validation, and automatic rollback on regression signals.
acceptance_criteria: Aggregated signal store exposes daily/hourly workload signatures (p90 seq len, arrival burstiness, affinity groups) for 90% of production routes.
Batch suggester produces deterministic suggested configs (max_batch, batch_timeout_ms, prefix_caching) and an estimated delta cost per 1M tokens.
Safe apply flow supports canary rollout to 5% of traffic, automated rollback on >5% latency or >10% quality regression.
End-to-end integration with Optimize recommender and Console dashboard with per-route diff and cost impact preview.
technical_notes: Workload encoder: sliding-window histograms + hashing-based fingerprint to group similar routes (retain privacy: only aggregated stats).
Model: lightweight XGBoost/regression for cost delta estimation; fallback heuristic rules for low-signal routes.
Sampling: adaptive sampler to retain rare long-tail requests for accurate tail latency.
Storage: store signatures in time-series DB (Prometheus/TSDB or ClickHouse) with retention of 90 days.
Safety: simulate new configs in a replay harness (nginx log replay -> runtime simulation) before canary.
Rollback: add circuit-breaker hooks in routing layer and integrate with rollout controller to auto-revert.
progress_updates: 2025-01-23: Kickoff meeting with Runtime and Optimize teams; scoped cross-team APIs and data contracts.
2025-01-28: Prototype encoder implemented; initial clustering reduces config space by ~62% on workoad-sample.
2025-02-03: Cost estimator model trained on 30k historical requests; RMSE within acceptable bounds for top-50 routes.
2025-02-09: Design review with Security and Privacy; approved aggregated-only telemetry and retention policy.
2025-02-11: First end-to-end canary plan drafted; documenting rollback thresholds and observability checks.
